overview_en: A Samoan wedding joins not just two people but two aiga. Protocol spans the church service, the fa'asamoa exchanges between the two families, and the seated meal that follows. The matai of each side speak; the families present 'ie toga and gifts; the new couple is formally received into both aiga.
overview_sm: O le faʻaipoipoga e le na o le tasi ma le tasi, ae o le tuʻufaʻatasiga o aiga e lua. E aofia ai le lotu, le faiga o le faʻasamoa i le va o aiga, ma le ʻaiga o loʻo sosoo ai. E lauga matai o itu e lua; e tuʻuina atu ʻie tōga ma meaalofa; ma e talia le ulugaliʻi fou i totonu o aiga uma.

roles.duty_en: Lead the formal exchange of speeches, gifts, and 'ie toga between the two families.
roles.duty_sm: E taʻitaʻi i le faʻafesāgaʻi o lauga, meaalofa, ma ʻie tōga i le va o aiga e lua.

roles.duty_en: Delivers the formal lauga on behalf of the matai and family.
roles.duty_sm: E fofogaina le lauga aloaʻia mo le matai ma le aiga.

roles.duty_en: Ceremonial children of the chief; carry honour at the reception and in the procession.
roles.duty_sm: Atalii ma afafine faʻaaloalogia o le matai; e amo le faʻaaloalo i le faʻafeiloaʻiga.

roles.duty_en: Contribute 'ie toga, money, and food; sit by side; honour the union by attendance and presentation.
roles.duty_sm: E saunia ʻie tōga, tupe, ma meaʻai; nonofo faʻavasega; faʻaaloalo i le mafutaga e ala i le auai ma le tuʻuina atu.

steps.body_en: Each family arrives together, led by their matai. Seating is by rank: matai forward, family behind. Wait to be welcomed before sitting; do not break the line.
steps.body_sm: E taunuʻu faʻatasi aiga taʻitasi, e taʻimua le matai. O le nofoa e faʻavasega: matai i luma, aiga i tua. Faʻatali seʻi talia oe ona nofo ai lea; aua le motusia le laina.

steps.body_en: The formal church wedding. Phones off. Respect the faife'au — stand and sit when the congregation does. Photography only where permitted.
steps.body_sm: O le lotu aloaʻia o le faʻaipoipoga. Tape telefoni. Faʻaaloalo i le faifeʻau — tu pe nofo pe afai e fai e le ekalesia. E naʻo le mea ua faʻatagaina e pueina ai ata.

steps.title_en: Fa'aulufalega and seating at the reception
steps.body_en: The couple and families are formally welcomed into the reception space. The two aiga sit facing each other; matai sit at the front of each line.
steps.body_sm: E talia aloaʻia le ulugaliʻi ma aiga i le nofoaga o le faʻafeiloaʻiga. E faʻafesāgaʻi nofoaga o aiga e lua; e nonofo matai i le itu i luma o laina.

steps.body_en: A tulafale from one side opens. The other side responds. Speeches honour God first, then the matai present, then the families, then the couple. Listen — do not interrupt.
steps.body_sm: E amata e se tulafale mai le tasi itu. E tali atu le isi itu. E faʻaaloalo muamua i le Atua, ona sosoʻo ai lea ma matai, aiga, ma le ulugaliʻi. Faʻalogo — aua le faʻalavelaveina.

steps.title_en: Si'i — exchange of 'ie toga and gifts
steps.title_sm: Siʻi o ʻie tōga ma meaalofa
steps.body_en: Each family lays out their 'ie toga, food, and money. A representative names each item as it is presented. The receiving side acknowledges and accepts. Quantity and quality of 'ie toga is noted in silence and remembered.
steps.body_sm: E faʻaali e aiga taʻitasi a latou ʻie tōga, meaʻai, ma tupe. E taʻu atu e le sui taʻitasi mea o loʻo faʻaali. E talia ma faʻafetai i le isi itu. E manatua le aofaʻi ma le mamalu o ʻie tōga e aunoa ma se tautala.

steps.body_en: A sua tray (cup, coconut, fine mat) is presented to the most honoured matai. Receive it with both hands and a quiet word of thanks; do not drink immediately.
steps.body_sm: E ofo atu se sua (ipu, niu, ʻie tōga) i le matai sili ona faʻaaloalogia. Talia i lima e lua ma se upu faʻafetai filemu; aua le inu vave.

steps.body_en: Wait until the matai have been served. Eat with dignity. The couple is served by the families. Do not leave the table until the lauga of thanks closes the meal.
steps.body_sm: Faʻatali seʻi tausami matai. ʻAi ma le faʻaaloalo. E tausi le ulugaliʻi e aiga. Aua le tulaʻi e seʻi oʻo ina maeʻa le lauga faʻafetai.

steps.body_en: A final lauga closes the function: thanks to God, to the families, to the matai. The couple is sent off with blessings. Do not leave before this.
steps.body_sm: E faʻaiʻu i se lauga: faʻafetai i le Atua, i aiga, ma matai. E tuʻuina atu faʻamanuiaga i le ulugaliʻi. Aua le tuʻua le sauniga aʻo leʻi maeʻa lenei vaega.

prepare_en: 'Ie toga (if you are aiga of the couple — speak to your matai about expected number and grade)
Cash contribution in an envelope marked with the giver's name
Food contribution if requested by your aiga
Arrive 30 minutes before the stated time
prepare_sm: ʻIe tōga (pe afai o oe o le aiga — talanoa i lou matai mo le aofaʻi ma le vasega)
Tupe i totonu o se teutusi ma le igoa o le tagata e tuʻu atu
Meaʻai pe afai ua tofia e lou aiga
Laʻei aloaʻia — vaʻai le Laʻei
Taunuʻu i le 30 minute aʻo leʻi amataina
wear_en: Women: puletasi or formal dress; head covered for the church service
Men: ie faitaga and white shirt with tie, or full suit
Avoid bright tourist prints, shoulders uncovered, or short hems
wear_sm: Tamaʻitaʻi: puletasi po o se ofu aloaʻia; pulou le ulu mo le lotu
Alii: ie faitaga ma se ofu paʻepaʻe ma le fusi ua, po o se suti atoatoa
Aua le ofuina o mea faʻaturisi, tatala tauʻau, po o ofu pupuʻu
mistakes_en: Sitting in front of the matai or in the matai row
Speaking during a lauga, even in a whisper
Photographing the si'i or sua without permission
Leaving before the closing lauga
Presenting an envelope without the giver's name on it
mistakes_sm: Nofo i luma o le matai pe i le laina o matai
Tautala i le taimi o le lauga e oo lava i le musumusu
Pue ata o le siʻi po o le sua e aunoa ma le faʻatagaina
Tuʻua le sauniga aʻo leʻi maeʻa le lauga faʻaiʻu
Tuʻuina atu se teutusi e leai se igoa o le tagata na foaʻi mai

overview_en: A Samoan funeral honours the deceased and supports the bereaved aiga over multiple days. It carries the heaviest fa'alavelave obligation. Where there is reconciliation to be made, an ifoga — a ceremonial act of contrition under a fine mat — may also take place.
overview_sm: O le maliu o se vaega tāua o le aganuʻu; e faʻaaloalogia ai e ua maliu ma fesoasoani i le aiga ua tigaina i aso e tele. O lenei o le faʻalavelave sili ona mamafa. Pe afai e manaʻomia se faʻaleleiga, e mafai ona faia se ifoga — o le tauʻolo i lalo o le ʻie tōga.

roles.role_sm: Aiga potopoto o le ua maliu
roles.duty_en: Receive condolences, manage protocol, and honour the deceased.
roles.duty_sm: E talia faʻafetai-alofa, faʻatautaia le tu, ma faʻaaloalogia le ua maliu.

roles.duty_en: Bring condolence (fa'aaloalo) — 'ie toga, money, food. Approach humbly.
roles.duty_sm: Aumai le faʻaaloalo — ʻie tōga, tupe, meaʻai. Faʻalatalata ma le lotomaualalo.

roles.duty_en: Receive each visiting party with the formal acknowledgement lauga.
roles.duty_sm: E talia e ia vaega taʻitasi ma le lauga faʻafetai.

roles.duty_en: Lead the church components: vigil, service, burial prayers.
roles.duty_sm: E taʻitaʻi lotu uma: po, sauniga, ma tatalo o le falelauasiga.

steps.body_en: News travels through the aiga, the church, and matai networks. If you hear from a matai of your aiga, attend or send representation; do not assume someone else will go.
steps.body_sm: E sosolo le tala i totonu o le aiga, le ekalesia, ma matai. Pe afai e te logo mai i se matai o lou aiga, alu ai pe auina atu se sui; aua le manatu e alu se isi.

steps.body_en: Visiting aiga arrive together, led by their matai. They walk in procession with 'ie toga held aloft. Stop at the gate; wait for the host tulafale to welcome you in.
steps.body_sm: E taunuʻu faʻatasi aiga asiasi, e taʻimua le matai. E savavali ma ʻie tōga sisi i luga. Tu i le faitotoʻa; faʻatali seʻi talia mai e le tulafale o le aiga.

steps.body_en: The host tulafale welcomes. The visiting tulafale offers a lauga of condolence: God, the deceased, the aiga, then the gift. The host receives.
steps.body_sm: E talia e le tulafale o le aiga. E lauga atu le tulafale asiasi: le Atua, le ua maliu, le aiga, ona sosoʻo ai lea ma le meaalofa. E talia e le aiga.

steps.title_sm: Siʻi — tuʻuina atu o le faʻaaloalo
steps.body_en: 'Ie toga are laid out; money envelopes named and counted aloud by a designated speaker; food set down. The aiga acknowledges.
steps.body_sm: E faʻaali ʻie tōga; e taʻuina aloaʻia teutusi tupe; e tuʻuina atu meaʻai. E faʻafetai atu le aiga.

steps.body_en: Where reconciliation is required, the offending aiga arrives at dawn, sits silently under fine mats outside the offended aiga's home until accepted. This is one of the most sacred acts in Samoan life — observe in silence; do not photograph.
steps.body_sm: Pe afai e manaʻomia se faʻaleleiga, e taunuʻu mai le aiga ua sese i le taeao po, nonofo filemu i lalo o ʻie tōga i fafo o le aiga ua sese i ai seʻi talia. O se tasi o sauniga sili ona paia o le aganuʻu — matamata ma le filemu; aua le pueina o ata.

steps.body_en: A church service is held, followed by burial — often in the family fanua. Family carry the casket; honoured guests follow.
steps.body_sm: E fai le sauniga a le ekalesia, ona sosoʻo ai lea ma le falelauasiga — masani lava i le fanua o le aiga. E amo le pusa e le aiga; e mulimuli mai le mamalu o le aoao.

steps.body_en: The aiga feeds those who travelled. Sit in your assigned area; wait for the matai. Speak softly.
steps.body_sm: E fafaga e le aiga i latou na malaga mai. Nofo i le mea ua tofia; faʻatali matai. Tautala lemu.

prepare_en: 'Ie toga (if your aiga is sending — confer with your matai)
Plan to stay for the lauga and meal, not just the burial
prepare_sm: ʻIe tōga (pe afai e auina atu e lou aiga — fesili i lou matai)
Tupe i se teutusi e i ai le igoa
Laʻei uliuli po o se lanu pogisa
Sao meaʻai pe afai e manaʻomia
Fuafua e nofo mo le lauga ma le taumafataga, ae le naʻo le falelauasiga
wear_en: Black or very dark conservative attire
Women: long puletasi or dress, shoulders covered, head covered for church
Men: black ie faitaga and white shirt with black tie, or dark suit
wear_sm: Tamaʻitaʻi: puletasi umi po o se ofu, pulou tauʻau, pulou le ulu mo le lotu
Alii: ie faitaga uliuli ma ofu paʻepaʻe ma fusi ua uliuli, po o se suti pogisa
mistakes_en: Loud talking, laughter, or phone use near the casket
Photographing an ifoga
Wearing bright colours or tourist prints
Arriving late or skipping the lauga to go to the burial only
Asking the bereaved aiga to entertain you
mistakes_sm: Tautala leotele, ata, po o le faʻaaogaina o telefoni i tafatafa o le pusa
Pue ata o se ifoga
Ofuina o lanu fiafia po o mea faʻaturisi
Tuai le taunuʻu pe naʻo le falelauasiga e te alu i ai
Faʻamalosi le aiga ua tigaina e tausi oe

overview_en: A saofa'i is the conferring of a matai title. The new matai sits with their aiga and the village council; the title is bestowed in front of the nu'u; an 'ava ceremony confirms it; the new matai is introduced to the village.
overview_sm: O le saofaʻi o le tuʻuina atu lea o se suafa matai. E nofo le matai fou ma lona aiga ma le fono a le nuʻu; e tuʻuina atu le suafa i luma o le nuʻu; e faʻamaonia i se sauniga o le ʻava; ma faʻailoa atu le matai fou i le nuʻu.

roles.duty_en: Confers the title and presents the new matai to the village.
roles.duty_sm: E tuʻuina atu le suafa ma faʻailoa atu le matai fou i le nuʻu.

roles.duty_en: Acknowledges and seats the new matai.
roles.duty_sm: E talia ma nofotūina le matai fou.

roles.duty_en: Provides the 'ie toga, money, food, and 'ava for the ceremony.
roles.duty_sm: E saunia ʻie tōga, tupe, meaʻai, ma le ʻava mo le sauniga.

steps.body_en: The aiga meets, agrees on the title and the candidate, and prepares the 'ie toga, food, and money for the village.
steps.body_sm: E fono le aiga, malilie i le suafa ma le sui, ma saunia ʻie tōga, meaʻai, ma tupe mo le nuʻu.

steps.body_en: The aiga walks in procession to the village maota. The candidate sits among them; the sa'o speaks first.
steps.body_sm: E savavali faʻatasi le aiga i le maota o le nuʻu. E nofo le sui i totonu o le aiga; e tautala muamua le saʻo.

steps.body_en: The 'ava is prepared and distributed. The new matai's cup is called by their new title for the first time. To answer to this call is to accept the title.
steps.body_sm: E saunia ma tufa le ʻava. E taʻua le ipu o le matai fou i lona suafa fou mo le uluaʻi taimi. O le tali atu o lona malilie i le suafa.

steps.body_en: Lauga are exchanged: the aiga thanks the village; the village welcomes the new matai; the new matai speaks last, humbly.
steps.body_sm: E faʻafesāgaʻi lauga: e faʻafetai le aiga i le nuʻu; e talia e le nuʻu le matai fou; e mulimuli le tautala a le matai fou, ma le lotomaualalo.

steps.body_en: 'Ie toga, money, and food are laid out. The village receives. A meal follows; the new matai serves the village.
steps.body_sm: E tuʻuina atu ʻie tōga, tupe, ma meaʻai. E talia e le nuʻu. E sosoo ai le taumafataga; e tausi e le matai fou le nuʻu.

prepare_en: Money — consult your sa'o on the amount
Formal la'ei for the candidate and aiga
prepare_sm: ʻIe tōga e tele (e faʻamoemoeina e le nuʻu)
Tupe — fesili i lou saʻo mo le aofaʻi
Puaʻa ma meaʻai (umu)
Aʻa o le ʻava
Laʻei aloaʻia mo le sui ma le aiga
wear_en: Candidate: ie faitaga (men) or formal puletasi (women)
Aiga: matching formal attire, modest and dignified
wear_sm: Sui: ie faitaga (alii) po o puletasi aloaʻia (tamaʻitaʻi)
Aiga: laʻei tutusa, faʻaaloalo, ma le mamalu
mistakes_en: Not consulting the full aiga before bestowing the title
Skimping on the village's expectations — the saofa'i is also a fa'alavelave
The new matai speaking first or speaking loudly
mistakes_sm: Le fesiligia o le aiga atoa aʻo leʻi tuʻuina atu le suafa
Le tau le mamafa i le faʻamoemoe o le nuʻu — o le saofaʻi o se faʻalavelave foi
Tautala muamua po o le tautala leotele a le matai fou

overview_en: The second Sunday of October — children lead the church service in white, perform recitations and songs, and are honoured by the aiga with a special meal. The day belongs to the children.
overview_sm: O le lua o Aso Sa o Oketopa — e taʻitaʻi e tamaiti le lotu, laʻei paʻepaʻe, e faʻaali tauloto ma pese, ma faʻaaloalogia e le aiga i se taumafataga faʻapitoa. O le aso e a tamaiti.

roles.duty_en: Lead readings, songs, and recitations. They are first in line at the meal.
roles.duty_sm: E taʻitaʻi tauloto, pese, ma faitauga. E muaʻi tausami.

roles.duty_en: Dress the children, prepare the meal, sit and watch with pride. Children are served first.
roles.duty_sm: E faʻamama tamaiti, saunia meaʻai, ma matamata ma le mitamita. E tausi muamua tamaiti.

roles.role_sm: Faifeʻau ma faiaʻoga o le aoga sa
roles.duty_en: Run the programme; rehearse the children; deliver the message for the day.
roles.duty_sm: E faʻatautaia le polokalama; e aʻoaʻoina tamaiti; ma tuʻuina atu le savali o le aso.

steps.body_en: White dresses, white shirts, white ie faitaga. Hair brushed. Shoes on. Bibles in hand.
steps.body_sm: Ofu paʻepaʻe, ie faitaga paʻepaʻe. Selu le ulu. Sevae. Faʻatasi le Tusi Paʻia.

steps.body_en: Songs, recitations of verses, and short messages. Even the smallest children participate.
steps.body_sm: Pese, faitauga o fuaiupu, ma savali pupuʻu. E auai uma tamaiti e oʻo lava i e laiti.

steps.body_en: A larger-than-usual Sunday lunch, with the children served and fed first.
steps.body_sm: O se toʻonaʻi lapoʻa, ma e muaʻi tausami tamaiti.

prepare_sm: Laʻei paʻepaʻe mo tamaiti uma
Tauloto pe pese ua sauni
Meaʻai e tele mo le toʻonaʻi
wear_en: White on every child; aiga in modest Sunday attire
wear_sm: Paʻepaʻe tamaiti uma; aiga i laʻei aso sa faʻaaloalo
mistakes_en: Forgetting to make this day primarily about the children
Sending a child without a verse to recite
mistakes_sm: Faʻagalo o le aso e mo tamaiti
Auina atu se tamaititi e leai sana tauloto

overview_en: The 'ava ceremony opens any formal gathering of matai. The 'ava root is pounded, mixed with water, and distributed in strict order of rank. It is a sacred act; treat it with the gravity given to communion.
overview_sm: E tatala e le sauniga o le ʻava soʻo se aofia o matai. E tuʻi le aʻa o le ʻava, palu i le vai, ma tufa i le faʻasologa o le mamalu. O se sauniga paia; e tatau ona faʻaaloalo e pei o le faʻamanatuga.

roles.duty_en: Pours and mixes the 'ava. Hands cleansed; movements deliberate.
roles.duty_sm: E sasaa ma palu le ʻava. Ua mama lima; e tatatau gāoioiga.

roles.duty_en: Daughter of a chief who, by tradition, prepares the 'ava in many villages.
roles.duty_sm: Afafine matai e faʻapea ona saunia le ʻava i nisi nuʻu.

roles.duty_en: Calls out each cup, naming the matai it is for in turn.
roles.duty_sm: E taʻuina ipu taʻitasi ma le suafa o le matai.

roles.duty_en: Receives the cup, performs the libation, drinks, returns the cup.
roles.duty_sm: E talia le ipu, faʻasusu, inu, toe tuʻu atu le ipu.

steps.body_en: The 'ava root is pounded and placed in the tanoa. Water is added; the taufa mixes by hand. Silence.
steps.body_sm: E tuʻi le aʻa o le ʻava ma tuʻu i le tanoa. E faʻaopoopo le vai; e palu e le taufa i le lima. Filemu.

steps.body_en: The tulafale names the most senior ali'i. The cup is carried to them by an attendant. Tradition determines which title is called first.
steps.body_sm: E taʻu e le tulafale le aliʻi sili. E ave le ipu e se tagata tausi. E faʻatatau i le aganuʻu poʻo ai e muaʻi taʻua.

steps.body_en: Receive with both hands. Pour a small libation onto the ground or into a coconut shell before drinking. Drink in one. Return the cup.
steps.body_sm: Talia i lima e lua. Sasaa se vaega itiiti i le eleʻele po o se ipu niu aʻo leʻi inu. Inu i le tasi sapasapaiga. Tuʻu atu le ipu.

steps.body_en: Ali'i first (in order of rank), then tulafale (in order of rank), then visitors and other matai. The order is precise; follow your tulafale.
steps.body_sm: Aliʻi muamua (i le faʻasologa o le mamalu), ona sosoʻo ai lea ma tulafale, ona sosoo ai lea ma malo ma isi matai. E saʻo lelei le faʻasologa; mulimuli i lau tulafale.

prepare_sm: Aʻa o le ʻava — ua mago lelei
Tanoa
Fau
Ipu
wear_en: Formal la'ei; covered shoulders; respect the gravity of the moment
wear_sm: Laʻei aloaʻia; tauʻau ua ufiufi; faʻaaloalo i le paia o le sauniga
mistakes_en: Drinking before the libation
Stepping over the fau or the tanoa
Talking while the cups are being distributed
Receiving with one hand or in a hurry
mistakes_sm: Inu aʻo leʻi faʻasusu
Sopo i luga o le fau po o le tanoa
Talanoa aʻo tufa ipu
Talia i le tasi le lima po o le faanatinati

overview_en: The Sunday meal after church. More than a meal — it is the weekly gathering of the aiga. The umu is cooked Sunday morning; the matai is served first; the children eat with the family or are sent to wait.
overview_sm: O le taumafataga o le Aso Sa ina ua maeʻa le lotu. E sili atu i se taumafataga — o le faʻapotopotoga o le aiga i lea vaiaso ma lea vaiaso. E vela le umu i le taeao Aso Sa; e muaʻi tausi le matai; e ʻai tamaiti ma le aiga.

roles.role_en: Cooks (often young men of the aiga)
roles.role_sm: Kuka (masani lava o talavou o le aiga)
roles.duty_en: Prepare the umu — taro, palusami, pork, fish — early Sunday morning.
roles.duty_sm: Saunia le umu — talo, palusami, puaʻa, iʻa — i le taeao Aso Sa.

roles.duty_en: Opens grace; is served first.
roles.duty_sm: E tatalo; e muaʻi tausi.

steps.body_en: Stones heated; food wrapped in leaves; covered with mats to cook.
steps.body_sm: Tao maʻa; afifi meaʻai i lau; ufitia i fala e vela ai.

steps.body_en: The aiga goes to church, then returns. The umu is opened; food is laid out.
steps.body_sm: E alu le aiga i le lotu, ona toe foi mai. E tatala le umu; e tuʻu i fafo meaʻai.

steps.body_en: The matai opens grace. Food is served to the matai first; then guests; then aiga.
steps.body_sm: E tatalo le matai. E tausi muaʻi le matai; ona sosoʻo ai lea ma malo; ma le aiga.

prepare_sm: Talo, palusami, iʻa, puaʻa
Maʻa ma fafie o le umu
Taimi — amata vave
wear_en: Sunday la'ei — keep the church attire on through the meal
wear_sm: Laʻei o le Aso Sa — faʻaauau le ofu o le lotu i le taumafataga
mistakes_en: Eating before the matai is served
Skipping grace
Not contributing to the cooking
mistakes_sm: ʻAi aʻo leʻi tausi le matai
Le faia o le tatalo
Le fesoasoani i le kuka

overview_en: A child's first birthday is a major Samoan family event — an occasion to thank God for the child surviving the most fragile year, and to formally introduce them to extended family. Expect a feast, a programme, and gifts.
overview_sm: O le aso fanau muamua o le tamaititi o se sauniga tāua i le aiga Sāmoa — o le faʻafetai i le Atua ona ola pea le tamaititi i le tausaga sili ona vāivai, ma le faʻailoa atu i le aiga atoa. E faʻamoemoe i se tausamiga, polokalama, ma meaalofa.

roles.duty_en: Host, feed, and present the child.
roles.duty_sm: Talimalo, tausi, ma faʻaali atu le tamaititi.

roles.duty_en: Speak blessings; present 'ie toga or cash.
roles.duty_sm: Fofogaina faʻamanuiaga; tuʻuina atu ʻie tōga po o tupe.

steps.body_en: The faife'au or family elder opens with prayer; parents welcome guests.
steps.body_sm: E tatalo le faifeʻau po o se toeaʻina o le aiga; e talimalo le mātua.

steps.body_en: Family members give speeches and blessings; children of the aiga perform.
steps.body_sm: E tautala ma faʻamanuia tagata o le aiga; e faʻaali pese e tamaiti o le aiga.

steps.body_en: The child is held by the parents; the cake is cut; gifts are received.
steps.body_sm: E talia e mātua le tamaititi; e tipi le keke; e talia meaalofa.

steps.body_en: A large meal follows; guests leave with takeaway plates if any are prepared.
steps.body_sm: E sosoo ai se taumafataga tele; e o ese malo ma ipu ave pe afai ua sauni.

prepare_sm: Keke ma teuteuga
Polokalama o lauga ma faʻaaliga
Meaʻai e tele
Pusa ave meaʻai
wear_en: Smart casual; family often coordinate colours
wear_sm: Laʻei tausaʻafia; e masani le aiga ona tutusa lanu
mistakes_en: Cutting the programme short — guests expect speeches
No takeaway plates
mistakes_sm: Faʻapuʻupuʻu tele le polokalama — e faʻamoemoe malo i lauga
Leai ni ipu ave meaʻai

overview_en: A graduation is celebrated by the whole aiga — it represents tautua repaid in success. Expect speeches, ula (lei), 'ie toga, and cash gifts. The graduate sits at the head with parents and grandparents.
overview_sm: E faʻamanatu e le aiga atoa le faʻauʻuga — o le faʻaiʻuga o le tautua ua taui mai. E faʻamoemoe i lauga, ula, ʻie tōga, ma meaalofa tupe. E nofo le ua faʻauʻu i le itu i luma ma mātua.

roles.duty_en: Receive blessings; speak final words of thanks at the close.
roles.duty_sm: E talia faʻamanuiaga; e tautala mulimuli ma le faʻafetai.

roles.role_en: Parents and matai of the aiga
roles.role_sm: Mātua ma matai o le aiga
roles.duty_en: Speak blessings; thank God and aiga; honour those who tautua'd.
roles.duty_sm: Fofogaina faʻamanuiaga; faʻafetai i le Atua ma le aiga; faʻaaloalogia e na tautua.

steps.body_en: A faife'au or family elder opens.
steps.body_sm: E tatala e se faifeʻau po o se toeaʻina o le aiga.

steps.body_en: Each branch of the aiga presents an ula to the graduate. The pile of ula is heavy by the end — this is the point.
steps.body_sm: E tuʻuina atu e ia paranesi o le aiga se ula i le ua faʻauʻu. E mamafa le faupuʻega o ula i le iʻuga — o le faʻamoemoega lea.

steps.body_en: Each elder speaks; cash and 'ie toga are presented and acknowledged.
steps.body_sm: E tautala ia toeaʻina; e tuʻuina atu ma faʻafetai tupe ma ʻie tōga.

steps.body_en: The graduate speaks last, briefly. Thank God, the aiga who tautua'd, parents specifically.
steps.body_sm: E tautala mulimuli ma le puʻupuʻu le ua faʻauʻu. Faʻafetai i le Atua, i le aiga na tautua, ma mātua patino.

prepare_sm: Meaʻai ma se faleoʻo mo tagata e 50–200
Faasolosolo o lauga
Ula e tele
Tagata pueata
wear_en: Graduate in regalia for part of the event; family in coordinated formal
wear_sm: Le ua faʻauʻu i le laʻei o le faʻauʻuga mo se vaega; aiga i laʻei tutusa aloaʻia
mistakes_en: Letting the graduate speak first or longest
Forgetting to thank those outside the immediate family who tautua'd
mistakes_sm: Tuʻu i le ua faʻauʻu e tautala muamua po o e umi tele
Faʻagalo e faʻafetai i tagata i fafo o le aiga vavalalata na tautua

overview_en: A church dedication is a major village and denominational event — months of fundraising culminate in a day of service, lauga, and feast. Expect village matai, visiting faife'au, and significant fa'alavelave.
overview_sm: O le faʻapaʻiaga o se falesa o se sauniga tāua i le nuʻu ma le lotu — masina e tele o sailiga o loʻo faʻaiʻu i se aso o le sauniga, lauga, ma le taumafataga. E auai matai o le nuʻu, faifeʻau asiasi, ma faʻalavelave mamafa.

roles.role_sm: Faifeʻau ma le fono a le ekalesia
roles.duty_en: Lead the dedication service.
roles.duty_sm: E taʻitaʻi le sauniga.

roles.duty_en: Receive visiting matai and faife'au, exchange formal lauga.
roles.duty_sm: Talia matai asiasi ma faifeʻau, faʻafesāgaʻi lauga.

steps.body_en: The visiting parties enter together; the village welcomes at the gate.
steps.body_sm: E ulufale faʻatasi mai aiga asiasi; e talimalo le nuʻu i le faitotoʻa.

steps.body_en: Prayer, scripture, anointing of the building, and dedicatory message.
steps.body_sm: Tatalo, tusi paʻia, faʻapaʻiaga o le fale, ma le savali.

steps.body_en: Visiting and host matai exchange lauga; 'ie toga, food, and money are presented and received.
steps.body_sm: E faʻafesāgaʻi lauga matai; e tuʻuina atu ʻie tōga, meaʻai, ma tupe ma talia.

steps.body_en: A village-scale feast follows. The new building is admired; speeches continue late.
steps.body_sm: E sosoo ai le taumafataga lapoʻa. E vaʻaia le fale fou; e faʻaauau lauga i le pō.

prepare_en: 'Ie toga and cash if your aiga is contributing
prepare_sm: ʻIe tōga ma tupe pe afai e tuʻuina atu e lou aiga
Laʻei aloaʻia
Onosaʻi — e umi
mistakes_en: Underestimating the fa'alavelave
Leaving early — the lauga continue until released
mistakes_sm: Le talitonu i le mamafa o le faʻalavelave
O ese vave — e faʻaauau lauga seʻi oʻo ina faʻamalolo

overview_en: Comedic theatre with deep roots — performers use humour to comment on village life, leadership, and behaviour. The faleaitu is permitted to speak truths nobody else can. Laugh, but listen.
overview_sm: Tausaʻafiga malie ma aʻa loloto — e faʻaaogaina e tagata faʻafiafia le malie e faʻamatala ai le olaga o le nuʻu, taʻitaʻiga, ma amio. E faʻatagaina le faleaitu e taʻu atu mea moni e leai se isi e mafai. ʻAta, ae faʻalogo.

roles.duty_en: Improvise sketches that satirise without crossing into open disrespect.
roles.duty_sm: Fai tausaʻafiga e ula ai ae le sopo i le le-faʻaaloalo.

roles.duty_en: Laugh openly; reward sharp commentary; do not take performance personally.
roles.duty_sm: ʻAta; tausia tagata faʻafiafia atamai; aua neʻi ita ai pe afai e patino atu.

steps.body_en: A short opening setting up the village or family being humoured.
steps.body_sm: O se amataga puʻupuʻu e faʻamatala ai le nuʻu po o le aiga e malie.

steps.body_en: Short, sharp scenes — often improvised — playing on stock characters and known village types.
steps.body_sm: Tausaʻafiga puʻupuʻu — masani lava ona faʻafuaseʻi — e faʻaali ai amio masani o le nuʻu.

steps.body_en: A formal close — performers thank the matai and the village.
steps.body_sm: Faʻaiʻuga aloaʻia — e faʻafetai tagata faʻafiafia i matai ma le nuʻu.

prepare_sm: Ofu — masani lava fai i le taimi
Iloa o tagata maʻoti o le nuʻu
wear_en: Whatever the role calls for — often deliberately ridiculous
wear_sm: Soʻo se mea e talafeagai — masani lava i mea mataʻiʻoa
mistakes_en: Crossing into open disrespect
Taking the satire personally as audience
mistakes_sm: Sopo i le le-faʻaaloalo
Ita ai i le tausaʻafiga pe a o oe le aoao
